---
title: "Download WEWoS"
---

WEWoS 0.1.0, the version described in our paper, is on GitHub:
[github.com/sannerlab/WEWoS](https://github.com/sannerlab/WEWoS) (tag
[v0.1.0](https://github.com/sannerlab/WEWoS/tree/v0.1.0)). Its core runs on Linux, macOS and
Windows with Python 3.7 to 3.13; the Molecules library and isocontouring need Linux.

## 1. Get WEWoS and its core

The core is the engine, the importer of Vision networks, and the Standard, 3D Visualization,
SymServer, Volume, Imaging and MatPlotLib libraries. It needs NumPy, Pillow and matplotlib:

```bash
git clone --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/sannerlab/WEWoS.git
cd WEWoS
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate     # or a conda environment
pip install -e ".[all]"
wewos check                                       # lists what is missing
```

The source is also available as an archive:
[WEWoS-0.1.0.tar.gz](https://github.com/sannerlab/WEWoS/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.0.tar.gz).

## 2. Add the molecular libraries (Linux)

The Molecules library needs MolKit2, ProDy (our fork), Open Babel and mslib (MSMS); isocontouring,
blurring and meshing in the Volume library need UTpackages. On Linux (x86_64) with Python 3.10 to
3.13, install what they need from PyPI, then the packages themselves from our package index:

```bash
pip install -e ".[all,molecules]"
pip install --no-deps --index-url https://sannerlab.github.io/pip/py3/ \
    molkit2==0.0.7 prody==0.0.5 bhtree==0.0.2 mglutil==0.0.5 mslib==0.0.2 utpackages==0.0.2
```

Use `--index-url` with these exact versions: `prody` and `mslib` are also the names of other
projects on PyPI.

With Python 3.7, they come with the `adcpsuite` environment that the
[ADCP 1.1 installer](../adcp/1.1/download.qmd) creates; `bin/wewos` finds that environment by
itself and runs WEWoS in it (`bin/wewos serve`, `bin/wewos check`).

## 3. Start WEWoS

```bash
wewos serve        # prints http://127.0.0.1:8767/?t=...  open it in your browser
```

The page needs a recent browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge) with WebGL; it loads nothing from
the internet. To run networks from other people in a sandbox, Linux needs bubblewrap
(`apt install bubblewrap`), macOS has what it needs, and Windows needs `wewos sandbox-setup` once.

To use WEWoS on a remote machine, start it there and forward its port from your computer:
`ssh -L 8767:127.0.0.1:8767 <host>`, then open the printed address.

The [documentation](documentation.qmd) and the [tutorials](tutorials.qmd) take it from there.
